en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove, from the Itthivimāna (The Female Vimānas)
3. The Story of the Mansion of the Provider of Water for Rinsing the Mouth "While you were wandering for alms,
standing there in silence;"
A woman poor and wretched,
who had never seen another's house,
gave you that gruel.
With her own hands she offered [the gift] with faith;
having abandoned her human body,
to which destination has she gone?
“As I was walking for alms,
standing there in silence,
a poor and wretched woman— ”
Not looking toward another's house:
she who gave me the rinsing-water with her own hands, full of faith.
Having abandoned the human body,
she passed away from here, fully liberated;
she is now known as a Nimmānarati deva.
“There are gods of great psychic power;
there that woman is happy,
rejoicing as one who gave the āma fruit.”
“Oh, how excellent is the gift of this poor woman!
It is well-established in the presence of Kassapa;
by means of this gift brought from elsewhere,”
Truly successful was that offering,
which would enable one to exercise the sovereignty of a Great Lord,
a Wheel-turning King.
A woman beautiful in all her limbs,
pleasing and delightful to her husband—
this is the result of this gift of fermented liquor.
It is not worth a sixteenth part of a single moment.
A hundred coins, a hundred horses,
and a hundred chariots drawn by mules—
A hundred thousand maidens,
adorned with earrings of strung jewels,
[are not worth a sixteenth part] of this gift of unboiled rice.
A hundred Himalayan elephants, with tusks like plow-poles and towering bodies, are not worth a sixteenth part of it.
The Mātaṅga elephants with golden girths,
clad in garments of refined gold— [all these are not worth a sixteenth part] of this gift of raw sugar.
It is not worth even a sixteenth part [of that merit].
Even if one were to exercise sovereignty over all four continents here, [it would not equal it].
"It is not worth even a sixteenth part of this gift of rinsing-water.
Thus ends the third Vimāna, the Ācāmadāyikā-vimāna.
